dirty_note: working tree carries the uncommitted internal/local package and the -local-search flags in solution/cmd/solve/main.go; this experiment flipped that flag's default from true to false
question: does the post-accept local search pay for itself on setB-01, where its per-call cost is no longer milliseconds?

solver_binary.solve.exe: built from this tree; arm ON used the then-default -local-search=true, arm OFF passed -local-search=false

arms.on: (no local-search flag: default true at the time of the run)

flags.ls_defaults: rounds=3 call_sec=3 budget_frac=0.20 top_cells=20 sat_min=0.01 probes=5

yardstick: cmd/diffsol between the two arms' solution files (no setB row exists in sprint_results/loads_vector.csv)

headline.diffsol: OFF wins at layer 1 (531282 vs 704559); full vector OFF-wins 3180 layers, ON-wins 45

determinism: both arms reproduce round for round on the repeat (OFF RESULT line identical in all three fields; ON identical in every ACCEPT/local line, differing only in the LS wall-clock seconds 1.917->1.963 and 1.485->1.647). The 704559 vs 531282 split is therefore not run-to-run noise.

cost.driver: local.tasks runs one UnitRoute per demand per surface slot per round; setB-01 is 6519 demands x 12 slots, so ~0.7-2e4 UnitRoute calls per round

decisions_taken: flipped -local-search default from true to false in solution/cmd/solve/main.go; the flag itself is kept
hypothesis_unverified: the split opens exactly where the LS hook calls dropMem() (LS improved the first bit at round 1, so the hook wipes done/seedMem/softFrozen and reschedules). An arm where LS is restricted to tail-only moves would test it; more repetitions would not, since determinism is already established.
caveat: one instance, one seed, one wall budget. Both ON runs were terminated (watchdog on run 1, manual on run 2), so no 'local: calls=... spent=...' summary exists and the LS share of the setB-01 wall clock is still unmeasured. Supports the default-off decision, not the stronger claim that LS is harmful on setB.
